guidance.pass: Headroom Safe: Microsecond spikes stay well within the 550W rail headroom.
guidance.warn: Heavy PSU Load: Peak spikes reach 75-95% of PSU capacity; fan will run loud.
guidance.fail: OCP Trip Risk: Microsecond transient spikes exceed 550W, risking emergency power shutdowns during intense scenes.

cpus.name: AMD Ryzen 5 5600GT
cpus.notes: Current system baseline. Solid Zen 3 APU with fast single-core clock, 16MB L3 cache.

cpus.name: AMD Ryzen 5 5600
cpus.notes: Dedicated Vermeer core with double L3 cache (32MB), offering ~10-15% higher 1% lows in RTS simulation games.

cpus.name: AMD Ryzen 7 5700X
cpus.notes: 8-core Vermeer AM4 drop-in upgrade with 65W TDP.

cpus.name: AMD Ryzen 7 5700X3D
cpus.notes: Ultimate AM4 gaming drop-in upgrade. Massive 96MB 3D V-Cache eliminates simulation frame dips in late-game RTS.

cpus.name: AMD Ryzen 5 7500F
cpus.notes: Value AM5 DDR5 gaming CPU without integrated graphics.

cpus.name: AMD Ryzen 5 7600
cpus.notes: Zen 4 platform upgrade path requiring DDR5 and AM5 motherboard.

cpus.name: Intel Core i5-13400F
cpus.notes: Hybrid 6P + 4E architecture with solid multi-threaded performance.

gpus.name: Radeon Vega 7 (Integrated)
gpus.notes: Base iGPU included with Ryzen 5 5600GT. Solid for esport RTS, requires lowest settings for heavy 3D.

gpus.name: GeForce GTX 1660 Super
gpus.notes: Popular used budget upgrade. Low 125W draw runs very cool on 550W PSU with 296W headroom.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 2060 (6 GB)
gpus.notes: Adds DLSS support and hardware ray tracing cores. Spikes stay comfortably below 320W.

gpus.name: Radeon RX 6600 (8 GB)
gpus.notes: The primary recommended upgrade champion. 8GB VRAM avoids modern stutter, 132W draw is ultra-safe for 550W PSU.

gpus.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (12 GB)
gpus.notes: 12GB VRAM great for VRAM-heavy textures and productivity; 170W TDP runs safe on 550W PSU.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4060 (8 GB)
gpus.notes: Ada Lovelace architecture. Extremely power efficient (115W TDP) with DLSS 3 Frame Generation.

gpus.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (8 GB)
gpus.notes: Strong 1080p/1440p Ada Lovelace card at 160W TDP with DLSS 3 Frame Generation.

gpus.name: Radeon RX 6700 XT (12 GB)
gpus.notes: 12GB VRAM powerhouse for 1440p. 230W TDP causes transient spikes to ~465W; runs close to 550W PSU comfort threshold.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4070 Super (12 GB)
gpus.notes: High performance 1440p card. Spikes to ~448W are tolerated on Tier A/B 550W, but PSU upgrade to 650W+ is recommended.

gpus.name: Radeon RX 7800 XT (16 GB)
gpus.notes: DO NOT RUN ON 550W PSU. 263W card exhibits microsecond transient spikes up to 526W (total system 611W), triggering OCP shutdown.

psus.name: 550W 80+ Bronze (43A Single +12V Rail)
psus.notes: Current baseline PC PSU. Safe <= 170W GPUs; 220W+ runs warm; >= 250W risks OCP trip.

psus.name: DeepCool PK550D 550W 80+ Bronze
psus.notes: Budget Tier-C DC-DC 550W PSU suitable for RX 6600 / RTX 4060 builds.

psus.name: Corsair CX650 650W 80+ Bronze
psus.notes: Safe headroom upgrade for 220W-230W GPUs like RX 6700 XT and RTX 4070 Super.

psus.name: MSI MAG A750GL PCIE5 750W 80+ Gold
psus.notes: ATX 3.0 compliant 2x excursion tolerance; handles RX 7800 XT (611W spikes) safely.
